title: The sultan who built the Court of the Lions
episode: The Alhambra of Granada and the Reign of Muhammad V
description: On Muhammad V, the Nasrid sultan who was overthrown, went into exile, and came back to rule Granada in the 1300s. He built the Court of the Lions and the halls around it, the most famous part of the Alhambra.
spotify: Wonders of the World The Alhambra of Granada and the Reign of Muhammad V
apple: Wonders of the World The Alhambra of Granada and the Reign of Muhammad V

title: The painted ceilings of the Hall of Kings
episode: The Paintings of the Hall of Kings at Alhambra, Spain
description: Art historian Ghadi Amer on the paintings on leather in the domes of the Hall of Kings, off the Court of the Lions. They show seated rulers, knights, and courtly scenes in a style that mixes Islamic and Christian painting.
spotify: The Multicultural Middle Ages Podcast The Paintings of the Hall of Kings at Alhambra, Spain
apple: The Multicultural Middle Ages Podcast The Paintings of the Hall of Kings at Alhambra, Spain

title: What Isabella and Ferdinand did with Granada
description: Historian Suzannah Lipscomb on how the Catholic Monarchs took Granada in 1492 and set out to make it a Christian city. They chose to be buried here, and their lead coffins lie in the crypt of the Royal Chapel.
spotify: Not Just the Tudors Isabella & Ferdinand's Granada
apple: Not Just the Tudors Isabella & Ferdinand's Granada

title: The Moriscos
episode: The Moriscos & the Purging of Muslim Spain (1492-1614) | Matthew Carr
description: Writer Matthew Carr on the Moriscos, the Muslims of Spain who were forced to convert after 1492. Those of the Albaicín, Granada’s old hilltop quarter, rose in revolt in 1568, and all Moriscos were expelled from Spain by 1614.
spotify: The afikra Podcast The Moriscos & the Purging of Muslim Spain (1492-1614) | Matthew Carr
apple: The afikra Podcast The Moriscos & the Purging of Muslim Spain (1492-1614) | Matthew Carr

title: Lorca
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on Federico García Lorca, the poet and playwright who mixed Andalusian folk tradition with the avant-garde. His family’s summer house, where he spent his last summer in 1936, is now a museum.

title: A local guide’s Granada
episode: Granada – Spain’s Moorish heart with Marta Sánchez from Bite Granada
description: A conversation with Marta Sánchez, a Granada-born tour guide, about her city: its neighborhoods, its history, and how its bars still serve a free tapa with every drink. Calle Navas is one of the busiest tapas streets.
spotify: When in Spain Granada – Spain’s Moorish heart with Marta Sánchez from Bite Granada
